# Instructor guide · Topic 2: Big-O Complexity

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Predict how running time and memory grow with input size, and know the cost of everyday Python operations.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **Big-O in plain words:** Big-O describes how the work grows as the input size n grows.
- **Count the steps:** You do not need maths to find a Big-O: count how many times the innermost line runs, and watch what happens when n doubles.
- **Spot the complexity:** Train your eye: loop shapes, halving, hidden loops inside built-in calls, and recursion.
- **How fast does it grow?:** Move the slider and compare how many steps each complexity needs, and roughly how long Python would take at about 10 million simple steps per second.
- **What Python operations cost:** Many one-liners hide a loop.
- **Space complexity:** Memory grows with n too.
- **From O(n²) to O(n):** Each problem has an obvious O(n²) answer with two loops.

## Duration and prerequisites

- Lessons: about **59 minutes** of guided material (7 lessons)
- Practice: 5 coding problems and 37 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 1 (Python for DSA)

## Live coding demonstrations

- See it: list vs set lookup (lesson “What Python operations cost”)
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Contains Duplicate: all pairs → set** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: How fast does it grow? · Growth curves · Count the steps

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- O(n²) to O(n) trick?
- Cost of lst.insert(0, x)?
- Cost of x in set?
- Two loops one after another?
- Binary search?
- Space complexity?
- String += in a loop?
- Recursion space?

### Teaching notes

- Set n to 1 million. Ask: which of these finish in under a second? Only O(1) to O(n log n). That is why interviewers push for better than O(n²).
- After the pair exercise, ask: what is the space cost? O(n) for the set. We traded memory for time, a trade-off that comes up constantly.

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Contains Duplicate (O(n)) (`bigo-has-duplicate`)
- Pair With Target Sum (O(n)) (`bigo-has-pair`)
- First Repeating Character (`bigo-first-repeat`)

Code tracing on the board: Count the inner steps (`bigo-p1`), Count the halvings (`bigo-p2`), Steps when n doubles (`bigo-p3`), Counting nested steps (`bigo-dr1`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- Optimize: Common Elements (`bigo-common`)
- Optimize: Count Pairs With Difference k (`bigo-count-pairs`)

## Homework

- For each exercise in topics 1–2, write its time and space complexity as a comment.
- Finish the topic's Review quiz in the browser and clear the revision queue.

## Solutions and grading

- Reference solutions: `solutions/02_bigo/` (also behind “Show solution” in the browser).
- Students check their own work with `python dsa.py test <id>`; collect `pytest tests/test_my_solutions.py -k bigo` output as evidence.
- Grade with the coding rubric in [README.md](README.md#grading-rubrics).
